- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.30) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a recent price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.30), model frequently underestimates downward moves; increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices, especially if sentiment turns negative.  
- Model tends to lag in recognizing short-term reversals; if sentiment shifts sharply from negative to neutral/positive, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections; apply a 2–3% upward bias to forecast if recent sentiment is negative and price has been trending down.
